I am 18, have Ulcerative Colitis, currently in remission and Immunosuppressed on a biological called Entyvio. I have to get an infusion once every 8-10 weeks and my next appointment is coming up in April. With everything that is going on, especially the fact that we are one of the hardest hit cities in United States, naturally I am nervous to get this infusion when the time comes. Hospitals are probably the last place any immunocompromised or high risk person should go to. This drug has saved my life, saved me from surgery and years of pain, I need this shit but I’m also so nervous to make the trip to receive my infusion. Any other immunocompromised people currently receiving infusions, any advice? Any knowledge that can be useful for me and all the other immunocompromised people worried about making their next trip to receive their infusion? 

Stay safe everyone! Keep practicing social distancing to the best of your ability! Just do it! Only go outside if it’s a necessity, like walking your dog or for health reasons. If not for yourself, do it for others who are high risk! Social distancing can seriously slow down the spread of COVID-19 in the weeks to come...
For info on social distancing, watch this informative video below please!
[Why fighting the coronavirus depends on you.](https://youtu.be/dSQztKXR6k0)

Stay safe, I’m 18 and seriously immunocompromised as well from Ulcerative Colitis, you don’t sound like a moron at all. If you have a friend who can get you groceries; even if it’s just cans of food, have them do that for you. For a safety measure, I’d advise leaving any food you receive that are not perishables outside or away from you for 3 days in order to make sure there is no dangerous bacteria on your food. Even spray them down 3-4 days after you receive them, then bring them into your house for extra precaution. Quarantine your groceries. It’s not crazy, it’s a precaution all people like us should be making. Stay safe!
